findings.title: Release identity is stale: attestation commit 9125913 != HEAD 38b34a9
evidence: docs/RELEASE_GATE.md:40 condition #1 'Re-attest the exact released HEAD'
findings.impact: The gate correctly refuses to call HEAD an attested release (commit_mismatch), but until the owner re-attests at 38b34a9 the release-integrity claim cannot be made.
findings.recommendation: Capture a fresh owner detached signature over the canonical identity at the released commit + migration head (0057) and the built image digests.
findings.note: Mechanism fixed by SEC-P1-001; the attestation content is stale at this HEAD.

findings.title: Operational reliability drills are not exercised per release
evidence: No dated drill/tabletop transcript under evidence/ for 38b34a9
DR-P3-001 / IR-P3-001 record the same gap from two lenses
findings.impact: Reliability controls are documented, not repeatedly exercised, so their per-release state is unproven.
findings.recommendation: Bind one restore drill + one tabletop to each release candidate and append the transcripts.

report: Final risk synthesis. The security core is sound and most 2026-10-03 P1 conditions are closed (branch protection, attested migration head, SBOM, signature-verified owner approval, version-controlled assurance schedule). The remaining release-integrity condition: the committed attestation covers commit 9125913, while HEAD is 38b34a9, so the runtime gate fails closed (commit_mismatch) and no attested release can be claimed at this revision. Verdict: GO WITH CONDITIONS for bounded runtime use; not an attested release.
